A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCR study and contain complete appendices. A Table 2 row visually obscured in v1 remains recoverable through text extraction, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original mechanistic experiments, head-selector evaluations, and TCR performance comparisons in Sections 3–5 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main accuracy comparisons and the additional experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: The head-localization measure, selector training objective, entropy-triggered intervention, head knockout, and majority-vote correction remain unchanged. The added takeaways summarize existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven primary tasks and retain the Big-GSM and reflective-reasoning evaluations in Appendices G.8–G.9. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: DoLa, random selection, Removing-and-Resampling, LOFIT, and direct base-model training retain their respective comparisons. The head-localization comparators in Appendix F.3 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, hop counts, training splits, test-instance counts, decoding settings, and entropy thresholds remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices D and G.

E4.justification: Both retain the same error breakdowns, head-knockout analyses, random-token controls, normalization comparisons, selector and majority-vote ablations, and case studies. The appendix analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report three-seed main accuracy averages, five-seed random-guessing results, and the same uncertainty reporting in Table 11. No run-count disclosure or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–12. For example, Table 2 retains Qwen2.5 average accuracies of 41.7% for the original model, 48.5% for TCR, and 61.3% for TCR-gold.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the CoT probability factorization, the selector objective, and the head-localization derivation in Appendix F.3 are retained without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about concentrated error types, competition between reasoning mechanisms, and TCR's effectiveness. The added resource-availability statement does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The new takeaways restate existing interpretations of head competition, shared erroneous heads, and predictive entropy. The substantive discussion and Appendix B limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future GitHub code release. v2 instead states that code and data are public and supplies a repository link in the abstract footnote. This improves access documentation; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 removes the introductory footnote contrasting explicit CoT with prior latent multi-hop reasoning studies, and removes Yang et al. (2024), 'Do large language models latently perform multi-hop reasoning?', from the references. The broader related-work discussion is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds five takeaway summaries, makes limited wording edits, updates affiliations and corresponding-author markers, and adds acknowledgements. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds bordered takeaway boxes, shortens Figure 3's caption, and relocates existing figures. Moving Figure 8 to the next page resolves its overlap with Table 2's final row in v1; the displayed results themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves usability through a concrete code/data access link, takeaway summaries, and a layout correction that makes Table 2's final row fully visible. These limited gains outweigh the small loss of related-work context. The methods, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
